slots.practicalActivity: In a free Developer Edition org, open Setup and create a new test user, noting that Profile and Role are two separate required fields; then open Object Manager -> Account -> Object Access tab and view the CRUD matrix across Profiles and Permission Set Groups to see the object/field layer and the record layer as genuinely separate systems.
slots.deliverable: A short written note (3-4 sentences) distinguishing "what a user can do" from "which records they can see," referencing the specific Setup screens where each is controlled.

slots.practicalActivity: In Object Manager, open the Account object's Object Access tab and compare CRUD (Create/Read/Edit/Delete) against View All/Modify All across at least two profiles or permission set groups; then create a custom permission set that grants Read and Edit on a custom object without Create or Delete, and assign it to a test user.
slots.deliverable: A custom permission set with Read+Edit (no Create/Delete) on one custom object, assigned to a test user, plus a one-sentence note on what View All/Modify All would have bypassed instead.

slots.practicalActivity: Clone a standard profile into a new custom profile in a Developer org, then explore its Login Hours, Login IP Ranges, and Password Policies settings; confirm that CRUD on a standard object is locked for the standard profile but editable on your new custom clone.
slots.deliverable: A new custom profile (cloned from a standard one) with a documented login-hours restriction and one CRUD permission changed from the original, with a note of what was locked on the standard profile that became editable on the clone.

slots.practicalActivity: Create two small, single-purpose permission sets (e.g., "Custom Object Edit Access" and "Report Export Access"), then build a Permission Set Group bundling both, and assign the group to a test user; check the group's Status column (Up to Date vs. Outdated) immediately after editing one of its member permission sets.
slots.deliverable: A Permission Set Group containing 2 member permission sets, assigned to a test user, with a note of the Status column's value before and after an edit to a member set.

slots.practicalActivity: On a custom object, create a new sensitive custom field (e.g., "Internal Risk Score"), then set Field-Level Security from the field itself (Set Field-Level Security in Object Manager) to grant Read+Edit to one profile and leave it fully unchecked for another; confirm Edit without Read isn't a persistable combination by testing it in the UI.
slots.deliverable: A new custom field with FLS configured differently across at least two profiles/permission sets, verified by Login As or a direct permission summary check.

lessons.title: How Profiles and Permission Sets Combine

slots.practicalActivity: Assign a test user a profile that doesn't grant Edit on a specific field, then assign them an additional permission set that does grant Edit on that same field; use Object Manager's Object Access tab (or Login As) to confirm their effective access is the union, not the profile's restriction.
slots.deliverable: A documented before/after: the test user's field access before the permission set was assigned (profile only) vs. after (union), with the Object Access tab notes showing both sources.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a complete "Sales Rep" access package from scratch in a Developer org: one custom profile (CRUD on a custom object), field-level security restricting one sensitive field to a narrower group, and one permission set granting an extra object's Edit access — then assign it all to a test user and verify effective access via Object Manager's Object Access tab.
slots.deliverable: One test user with a custom profile + FLS configuration + one permission set assigned, and a written summary of that user's effective access across the object and the sensitive field.

slots.practicalActivity: Without re-reading the lessons, sketch (on paper or in a doc) the object/field-access stack from Chapter 1: profile -> permission sets/groups -> field-level security -> effective access union; then verify your sketch against Object Manager's actual Object Access tab for a real object in your org.
slots.deliverable: A one-page diagram or written summary of the Chapter 1 object/field-access model, checked against a live object's Object Access tab for accuracy.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup's Sharing Settings, change a custom object's OWD through the three-question decision framework (who's most restricted, can they see everything, can they edit everything) and set Private, Public Read Only, or Public Read/Write accordingly for both Internal and External Access.
slots.deliverable: A documented OWD decision for one custom object, with the three-question reasoning written out and the actual Internal/External Access settings configured in Sharing Settings.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a 3-level role hierarchy in Setup (e.g., Manager -> Team Lead -> Rep), assign test users to each role, set the custom object's OWD to Private, and confirm via Login As that a Manager-role user can see records owned by a Rep below them but a peer Rep cannot see another peer's records.
slots.deliverable: A 3-level role hierarchy with test users assigned, verified via Login As that upward visibility works and lateral (peer-to-peer) visibility does not.

slots.practicalActivity: With the custom object's OWD set to Private, create one owner-based sharing rule (sharing one group's records with another group) and one criteria-based sharing rule (sharing records matching a field value with a different group); confirm via Login As that both widen access as expected without affecting OWD itself.
slots.deliverable: Two active sharing rules (one owner-based, one criteria-based) on the same custom object, each verified with a test user via Login As.

slots.practicalActivity: Manually share one specific record with a single test user via the record's Share button, then change that record's owner and confirm (by checking the Sharing Detail view) whether the manual share survived the ownership change or was removed.
slots.deliverable: A documented before/after of one manually-shared record's sharing list, showing what happened to the manual share after an ownership transfer.

slots.practicalActivity: Add an Opportunity Team to a test Opportunity with at least two members, each with a distinct Team Role and Access Level (one Read Only, one Read/Write); then configure a Default Team for your own user and use Add Default Team on a second Opportunity to confirm the team is added automatically.
slots.deliverable: Two Opportunities — one with a manually-built team, one populated via Add Default Team — each showing per-member Team Role and Access Level.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Public Group containing a mix of individual users and a role, use it as the recipient of a sharing rule from the previous lesson's slot; then separately create a Queue scoped to a custom object, add members, and manually assign a record into the queue to confirm a queue member can accept it.
slots.deliverable: One Public Group used as a sharing-rule recipient, plus one working Queue with at least one record sitting in it ready to be claimed.

lessons.title: Controlled by Parent and Grant Access Using Hierarchies

slots.practicalActivity: Inspect the OWD page for Contact and confirm it reads "Controlled by Parent"; test this by changing a test user's access to a specific Account and confirming their access to that Account's child Contacts changes identically without any Contact-specific sharing configuration.
slots.deliverable: A documented test showing a user's Contact access changing in lockstep with their Account access, with no separate Contact-level sharing rule involved.

slots.practicalActivity: Design and build the full Chapter 2 record-access stack on one custom object end to end: Private OWD, a role hierarchy with at least 2 levels, one sharing rule pointing at a Public Group, and a manual share on one record — then verify the whole stack with Login As for three different test users (a peer, a manager, and a sharing-rule recipient).
slots.deliverable: One custom object with all four Chapter 2 mechanisms configured together, verified via Login As for 3 distinct users with 3 different expected outcomes.

slots.practicalActivity: Diagram the full record-access stack from OWD at the bottom up through role hierarchy, sharing rules, and manual sharing/teams at the top, labeling which mechanisms only widen access and never narrow it; cross-check the diagram against the actual Sharing Settings page for a real object.
slots.deliverable: A labeled stack diagram of OWD -> role hierarchy -> sharing rules -> manual sharing/teams, verified against a live Sharing Settings page.

lessons.title: Designing Security for a Sales Organization

slots.practicalActivity: Using the Meridian Outfitters scenario as a template, design and build the equivalent security model for your own test org: Private OWD on a custom "Deal" object, a matching role hierarchy, one sharing rule for a support-style group, and one permission set for a manager-level privilege.
slots.deliverable: A built-out sales-org security design (OWD + role hierarchy + 1 sharing rule + 1 permission set) on a test object, with a one-paragraph write-up of the OWD decision.

lessons.title: Designing Security for a Service Organization

slots.practicalActivity: Build the Harbor Point Support pattern on a custom "Support Ticket" object: Public Read Only OWD, a Queue for unassigned tickets, and a case-team-style escalation (add a second user to a ticket's sharing with Read/Write while the first keeps Read Only) when a ticket escalates.
slots.deliverable: A custom object configured with Public Read Only OWD, a working queue, and a documented escalation test showing both the original and escalated user retaining appropriate access.

lessons.title: Restriction Rules and Scoping Rules Overview

slots.practicalActivity: On a custom object (or a supported standard object like Events/Tasks), build a Restriction Rule that narrows a defined group of users down to records matching specific criteria, even though a sharing rule already grants them broader access; confirm via Login As that the restriction rule actually narrows what that group sees.
slots.deliverable: An active Restriction Rule verified with Login As to narrow a test user's visibility below what OWD/sharing alone would grant.

lessons.title: Testing Security with Login As and Run As

slots.practicalActivity: Enable "Administrators Can Log In as Any User" in Login Access Policies, then Login As three different test users built in earlier chapters and run through the Lesson 17 testing checklist for each (list what they should/shouldn't see, then verify); separately, write one simple Apex test using System.runAs() against one of those users to confirm a sharing rule's effect in code.
slots.deliverable: A completed testing checklist for 3 test users verified via Login As, plus one passing Apex test using System.runAs().

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately misconfigure one piece of your test org's access (e.g., set a case-team role template to grant Read instead of Edit), then work through the layered troubleshooting order (object permissions -> FLS -> OWD -> hierarchy -> sharing -> restriction rules) to diagnose and fix it, using the user's permission summary and the record's sharing detail view.
slots.deliverable: A written troubleshooting log naming the deliberately broken layer, the diagnostic steps taken in order, and the specific fix applied.

slots.practicalActivity: Audit your own test org (built across this chapter) against the five common mistakes — Public Read/Write defaults, View All/Modify All shortcuts, profile explosion, sharing-rule patching, and no access review — and note which, if any, crept into your own configuration.
slots.deliverable: A short self-audit (one line per mistake) stating whether it's present in your test org and, if so, the specific fix you'd apply.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the Brightwell Insurance Group case study as a model, write your own 4-finding audit report for a hypothetical org of your choosing, prioritizing findings by data sensitivity and current exposure (not ease of fix), each with an actionable audit note in the same style as the lesson's examples.
slots.deliverable: A written 4-finding security audit report with findings prioritized and each finding stating the gap, the recommendation, and the reasoning.

slots.practicalActivity: Combine Chapters 1-3 into one end-to-end lab: pick either a sales-org or service-org shape, build the complete security model (OWD, role hierarchy or queues, 2 sharing rules, 1 restriction rule, 2 permission sets) in a Developer org, then run the Lesson 17 testing checklist against 3 test users and fix any gap you find using the layered troubleshooting order.
slots.deliverable: A fully built, tested security model in a Developer org (OWD + hierarchy/queues + sharing + restriction rule + permission sets) with a written testing log showing at least one bug found and fixed.

slots.practicalActivity: Review your capstone lab against the common-mistakes checklist and the audit-priority framework; write a short "if I audited this org" paragraph identifying the single biggest remaining risk in your own design and how you'd prioritize fixing it.
slots.deliverable: A one-paragraph self-audit of your own Chapter 3 lab, naming the single highest-priority remaining risk and its fix.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup's Sharing Settings, change an object's OWD from Public Read/Write to Private (or vice versa) on a test object with existing records, click Recalculate next to any affected sharing rule, and note how long recalculation takes and whether Login As immediately reflects the new model.
slots.deliverable: A documented before/after OWD change with the Recalculate action triggered, and a note of whether access appeared to update immediately or needed time to catch up.

lessons.title: Guest User and Community Security Overview

slots.practicalActivity: If you have access to an Experience Cloud site or Salesforce Site, open its Guest User profile and review every object permission granted; remove anything not required by the site's actual public forms, confirm API Enabled is off, and set up a Sharing Set (rather than a broad sharing rule) for one object the guest user needs record access to.
slots.deliverable: A guest user profile audited and tightened (object permissions reviewed, API Enabled confirmed off), with one Sharing Set configured for a specific object instead of a broad sharing rule.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup's Session Settings, review and document the current Session Timeout, Force Logout on Session Timeout, and Lock Sessions to IP Address settings; then run Health Check and address at least one medium- or high-risk finding it surfaces.
slots.deliverable: A documented session-settings configuration plus a Health Check score with at least one finding fixed directly from the dashboard.

lessons.title: Preparing for the Sharing and Visibility Architect Path

slots.practicalActivity: Rebuild the Lesson 14 Meridian Outfitters design from scratch in your Developer org (OWD, role hierarchy, 2 sharing rules, 3 permission sets) without referring back to the lesson text, then verify it with Login As; deliberately introduce one common mistake and use the layered troubleshooting order to find and fix it yourself.
slots.deliverable: A from-memory rebuild of the Meridian Outfitters security design, verified via Login As, plus a documented find-and-fix of one deliberately introduced mistake.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page portfolio summary of the complete security model you built across this course (profiles, permission sets, FLS, OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rules, restriction rules, guest user hardening, session settings), including notes on the key configuration screens, ready to show to an employer.
slots.deliverable: A one-page portfolio write-up covering the full security model built across the course, with notes on each configuration area.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can design, build, and verify a complete Salesforce record-access and object/field security model — profiles, permission sets, field-level security, OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rules, restriction rules, and session/guest-user hardening — for both sales-style and service-style organizations, and can audit an existing org's security configuration for real risks.
